messages:
sophia: quick FYI — ran int4 conversion of GemmaX 6.7B -> our qwen-compatible weights and saw a reproducible dip on arithmetic benchmark when input has a prefix that ends with a newline + EOS-like token.
max: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro?
sophia: reproducer below, short prompt pipeline: tokenizer(vocab-shrunk) + conversion script that does per-head folding. failing case: prefix = 'Question:\n' then system EOS appended by our harness.

sophia: command: 
```
./convert_weights --src gemmax6b --dst qwen-compat --quant int4 --grouped 16 --preserve-eos --rotary-base auto
python run_eval.py --model converted.pt --prompt-file tests/prefix_eos.txt --seed 42
```

alice: did you try forcing rotary-base to the original GemmaX value?
sophia: yes — when I force rotary_base to 10000 (GemmaX default) the regression disappears. if left on auto, the converter picks 2048 and we get the drop.
max: interesting. so mismatch between rotary scaling and tokenizer/vocab shrink step causes probability mass shift at token boundary?
sophia: exactly. digging into logits: tokens crossing a BPE split (like "-ing" joined across prefix) have shifted phase, small but enough to flip argmax on math steps.
max: any evidence on KV-cache or just immediate next-token?
sophia: both. KV cache shows gradual phase drift after 8 tokens when the prefix included an EOS-sentinel. embedding cosine distance between converted and baseline grows ~0.03 after 10 steps in the failing trace.
eval-bot: run id 2024-11-02-1743: math-bench/median-accuracy went 0.87 -> 0.65 on int4-auto-rotary, float16 baseline 0.88.
alice: do we see per-head gain mismatch? can we dump per-head rotary multipliers?
sophia: yes — conversion log: "head_gain[12]=1.004" vs expected ~0.999 for many heads. looks like a float->int calibration rounding in grouped quant path.
max: hypothesis: our vocab-shrinking step reindexes tokens and also trims some sentinel codepoints; converter's auto-rotary heuristic recomputes base from seq-len stats which are skewed by removed tokens -> wrong frequency mapping -> small phase leak.
alice: practical workaround for rollout: add --rotary-base override in converter and mark sensitive eval suites to skip int4-auto. does quant calibrator we ship support per-head rescale?
sophia: not currently. quick fix: run an affine per-head rescale post-conversion using a tiny calibration set (100 sequences) to match float16 head-wise mean activations. script: 
```
# pseudo
for h in heads:
  scale[h] = mean_fp16_kv[h] / mean_int4_kv[h]
  weights_q[h] *= scale[h]
```
# then re-eval
```

max: small question — is this specific to GemmaX -> Qwen or seen with Llama/Mistral conversions?
sophia: tried Llama->Qwen path quickly, no obvious regression. Mistral case shows milder effects but only when we do vocabulary compaction (our shrinker) + grouped int4. seems GemmaX's rotary parameterization is more sensitive.
alice: ok can you open a ticket with the conversion run id, attach diffs of rotary_base chosen, and label as "high-priority eval-regression"? link to fix: suggest adding a converter flag --force-rotary-base and adding a small per-head calibration pass to Optimize.
sophia: will do. adding short checklist in ticket: reproduce command, eval logs, head_gain dump, per-head rescale patch, and mitigation note to ops to default int4-auto OFF for GemmaX families until patched.
eval-bot: ticket created: RIN-5421.
max: nice triage. one more thing — add a unit test to our eval harness that runs prefix+newline cases through all conversion presets, so we catch this in CI.
sophia: on it. thanks all :thumbsup:
